Sfenj for Hanukkah

Moroccan · Medium · Makes about 15 sfenj

Jump to Recipe Method Troubleshooting Storage
The sfenj's festival seat: the #6 master record's same wet dough, the same hollow fry, the same ten-minute window — carried into the Hanukkah week, when the frying itself is the mitzvah and the oil's miracle is celebrated in every kitchen's pot. The Sephardic communities of Morocco fried sfenj for the festival's eight nights; the master record carries the craft, and this seat carries the occasion — the doughnuts of the oil's remembrance.

Quantities live in the recipe card.

Ingredients

  • the wet, sticky dough and its 1½-hour rise, the whole craft
- **The #6's laws carried whole:** the wet dough kneaded with oiled hands, the full rise, the plum-sized piece shaped by palm and two fingers straight into the oil, the float-and-puff in 20 seconds, and the 2–3 minutes' fry to the deep gold. Read the master record for the full checkpoints; the festival's own work is the occasion's service. - **The festival's bridge:** none needed — the sfenj runs its own truth, and the Hanukkah week's frying is the tradition's own permission to make the everyday's doughnut the celebration's own.

Sfenj for Hanukkah

Prep: 20 min (plus 1 h rise) · Cook: 20 min · Total: 1 h 40 min · Makes about 15 sfenj

Ingredients

Ingredients

  • The #6 master record's dough: 400 g flour, ½ tsp salt, 1 tsp sugar (about 4 g), 1 tsp instant yeast (about 4 g), 320 ml lukewarm water — the wet, sticky dough and its 1½-hour rise, the whole craft
  • Neutral oil for the frying, 4 cm deep at 180 °C
  • The festival's finishes: caster sugar (about 100 g), the cinnamon-sugar mix, or the honey's warm drizzle; and the #116 cumin salt for the heretical savory handful
  • The #119 mint tea's pot, sweet, for the sfenj's own service

Instructions

  1. **The dough and the rise, per the #6** — the wet dough, the oiled bowl, the full 1½ hours to the doubled, glossy top. Checkpoint — the #6's own: puffed, glossy, still sticky — the dough that fries to the hollow.
  2. **The festival's frying, in rounds.** The oil at 180 °C, the shaped rings fried in the small batches — the #6's whole craft, run in the celebration's generous rounds: the first batch for the children's waiting hands, the second for the table's gathering, the pot never cold through the evening. Checkpoint — the #6's law: the hollow's puff, the deep gold's blister, the 2–3 minutes' ceiling — and the festival's own addition: the frying's eight nights, the oil's abundance, the miracle's remembrance in the kitchen's own heat.
  3. **The sugar's coat and the tea's service.** The hot sfenj rolled in the sugar (or the honey's drizzle, or the cinnamon's mix), eaten in the ten-minute window, the mint tea's sweet pot beside — the festival's own complete service. Checkpoint — eating test: the #6's own — the crackle's shatter, the hollow's steam, the soft strands within — the sugar's sweetness over the dough's faint salt, the tea's mint cutting. On the Hanukkah night it should taste like the tradition's own argument: the oil that burned eight nights, fried into the doughnut that remembers them, and the family's table the festival's whole venue.

Troubleshooting

SymptomCauseFix
See the #6's tableThe one dough, the one craftThe master record's rows carry

Storage, Make-Ahead & Variations

- The #6's own: made and eaten in the window, the dough holding a day refrigerated after its rise. The festival's week runs the nightly batches. - Variations: the honey's drizzle finish, the jam-filled's luxury. The #6 sfenj is the master; the #71 fijuelas are the festival's other fried seat on this site.
